problem: Long-horizon robot agents conflate a model's proposed progress, a controller's 'done' signal, and verified task completion, so false completion and stale or misbound evidence corrupt downstream decisions. Existing execution loops and verifiers do not specify which component may change trusted task state or which evidence each role may see.
motivation: As task length grows, task success is a product of stage probabilities, so an early false-positive completion corrupts every later step. Physical skills return when a command is accepted or a controller stops, not when the intended effect holds. The paper therefore separates authority (propose, execute, verify, commit) and adds a cross-mission self-improvement loop that revises only the harness configuration.
key_idea: An evidence-gated robot-agent harness in which only an identity- and version-bound commit gate can advance trusted task state, with role-isolated contexts, budgeted recovery, and a cross-mission RSI protocol that revises harness configuration under fixed regression checks.
insight: The circuit case shows completion depends on execution history: the robot starts about 0.23 m from the goal, inside the 0.40 m arrival tolerance, yet the task requires departure, route progress and return. Endpoint proximity or a controller 'done' signal is therefore not enough, which motivates the node-level and goal-level verifiers. The paper contains no ablations or quantitative comparisons, so the claimed benefits for false completion, duplicate dispatch and RSI are only defined as a protocol and not measured.
method: Model loop vs agent loop: model-backed roles compile a context and emit proposals; the agent loop dispatches, observes, verifies, commits and recovers. Tool return, node acceptance and goal completion are distinct stopping conditions.
Role-isolated contexts C1-C4: a software compiler builds planner, skill, verifier and recovery views from versioned memory. The verifier excludes the planner's completion claims.

Typed task contracts and capability cards: a dependency graph of nodes with target effects, and provider cards with preconditions, side effects, cancellation and evidence needs. Deterministic filtering is followed by a configurable scorer over success, risk, uncertainty, latency, cost and history.
Supervised skill lifecycle: idempotent dispatch keyed by task/node/state version, time-bounded resource leases, deadlines and persisted handles.

Evidence packets, verification and commit gate: a packet holds identities, state version, before/after observations, pose and proposed facts. Node verifiers return satisfied/violated/ambiguous, the gate atomically commits, and a goal verifier rechecks the original user goal.
Budgeted recovery (C4): failure classes map to escalation ladders (re-perceive, replan, switch skill, safe stop, human handoff), each action consuming per-action and total budgets.

Evidence-gated RSI: candidate revisions to context rules, templates, routing and recovery are generated from traces and checked on a fixed regression set. Release requires an acceptance predicate, rollout happens at mission boundaries with rollback, and the updater cannot weaken the commit gate.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-Plus (frozen, visual analysis); Qwen-Plus (frozen, text planning in the camera task); VLM for exploration goal selection; streaming ASR; the navigation stack is a classical planner (omni_planner)
setting.observation: quadruped onboard camera images (1280x720 panoramas), LiDAR SLAM point-cloud map and pose, microphone audio
setting.action_space: supervised velocity interface with a fixed reference route and local planner (0.5 m/s cap, 0.6 m lookahead); rotation segments
setting.privileged: none (configured place anchors A and B and a saved point-cloud map are used)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark results. Only real-robot case measurements (endpoint distances, path lengths) are reported. The planned controlled harness comparison, ablations and RSI evaluation are defined as a protocol, with no results.
results: On one real voice-triggered warehouse inspection the seven-stage workflow completed. Outbound and return endpoint errors were 0.11 m and 0.17 m, and mission execution took 259.94 s (271.22 s for the full voice turn). Table 1 lists reference path lengths of 17.62 m and 18.83 m and arrival distances of 0.11, 0.17 and 0.25 m against a 0.40 m tolerance. No baselines were compared and no quantitative gains are reported.
limitations: Evidence is anecdotal: a few single-run real-robot cases with no baselines, ablations, or measured false-completion, duplicate-dispatch or RSI results.
The RSI protocol is specified but not demonstrated; there is no run showing a candidate revision, regression results, release or rollback.
Reference runtime is single-host with synchronous-cancel lease assumptions; verification quality depends on sensors and correlated errors, and exact model-decision replay is not guaranteed.
